clue.text: Drivers get lessons on this landscaped area

definitions.text: Drivers get lessons on this landscaped area

parts.note: reads like learner motorists being taught, but drivers are also the long-hitting clubs used off the tee
the shaped and planted ground where those clubs are swung

explanation.surface: Learner drivers take their lessons out on some landscaped piece of ground.
explanation.walkthrough: A driver is the golf club used for the longest shots, and players take lessons from a club professional on the course itself.
explanation.definitionFit: A golf course is a large tract of land shaped into fairways, greens and bunkers for playing golf.

clue.text: Having change of heart, snatch dress

indicators.note: the heart of the word for snatch, its two middle letters, changes places, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: to snatch is to grab

explanation.surface: Someone changes their mind and snatches up a dress after all.
explanation.walkthrough: Only the two central letters swap; the outer letters stay put.
explanation.definitionFit: Garb is clothing or attire, so it serves as the noun for what one wears.

clue.text: Charlie admits soft spot — quite the reverse in defeat

indicators.note: one piece letting another in signals insertion
it is the soft spot that takes in Charlie, not the other way round

parts.note: a soft spot for something is a liking for it

explanation.surface: Charlie confesses to having a weakness, though the opposite turns out to be true in the loss.
explanation.walkthrough: Read literally, Charlie would hold the soft spot; the reversal instruction swaps container and contents.
explanation.definitionFit: A licking is informal for a heavy beating or thrashing in a contest.

clue.text: Succeed as a chum strutted outrageously

indicators.note: behaving outrageously means acting wildly, so these letters are thrown into disorder

parts.note: taken as written, these letters are the material to rearrange

explanation.surface: A pal makes it, swaggering about in an outrageous fashion.
explanation.definitionFit: To cut the mustard is an idiom for meeting the required standard, that is, being good enough.

clue.text: In full, a generation's waste

indicators.note: the answer sits inside the run of words that follows

parts.note: taken as written, the answer runs across these words

explanation.surface: In full, the wastefulness of a whole generation.
explanation.walkthrough: Ullage is the amount by which a cask or bottle falls short of full, through leakage or evaporation.
explanation.definitionFit: Ullage names liquid lost from a container, so it is a kind of loss or wastage.

clue.text: This term seems to fly with one month gone?

definitions.text: This term seems to fly with one month gone?

indicators.note: letters made to fly are scattered and land in a new order
something gone is taken away, here from the word term

parts.note: taken as written, before one letter is dropped
M is the standard abbreviation for month
taken as written

explanation.surface: A student finds the teaching term racing by, a month already behind them.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue defines too: a semester is a half-year term, and terms do seem to fly by.
explanation.definitionFit: A semester is one of two halves into which an academic year is divided, a teaching period.

clue.text: Postgrad's time is nuts

parts.note: an MA is a postgraduate degree holder, so a postgrad's is MA's

explanation.surface: A postgraduate student's schedule is crazy.
explanation.walkthrough: Nuts is not the slang for mad here: mast is the fallen fruit of beech, oak and similar forest trees.
explanation.definitionFit: Mast is the collective name for beechnuts, acorns and similar nuts lying on the forest floor.

clue.text: Coffee — a current one watering-hole picked up

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: in a down answer, picking something up raises it, so the pieces read from bottom to top

parts.note: AC is alternating current
a bar is where one goes for a drink

explanation.surface: A coffee is fetched from a bar while a current flows.
explanation.definitionFit: Arabica is the main species of coffee plant and the beans it yields.

clue.text: Cross with tutors ignoring the compiler's doggerel, say

indicators.note: ignoring something means leaving it out of the verb for tutors

parts.note: to tutor someone is to train them
the compiler is I, the setter speaking of themself
doggerel is an example of verse, poor and comic

explanation.surface: Teachers are annoyed because they skip over the setter's bad poetry.
explanation.walkthrough: Cross is an adjective meaning lying across, not angry as the surface suggests.
explanation.definitionFit: Transverse describes something lying or extending across, at right angles to the main axis.

clue.text: Reading article with a new slant

indicators.note: giving something a new slant changes its angle or arrangement, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written, these letters are the material to rearrange

explanation.surface: A journalist reads out a piece of writing given a fresh angle.
explanation.definitionFit: A recital is a public reading or performance, such as a poetry recital.

clue.text: Motor belonging to mother with a coloured liner

parts.note: mother is MA, so her motor is MA'S CAR
taken as written

explanation.surface: Mum's car comes with a coloured paint stripe.
explanation.walkthrough: Liner suggests a ship or a car's trim, but it is make-up applied to the eyelashes.
explanation.definitionFit: Mascara is cosmetic colouring brushed onto eyelashes, a tinted lining for the eyes.

clue.text: Sine qua non of Stoicism? Being strong on superior insolence

parts.note: a stiff drink or breeze is a strong one
upper means higher or superior in rank
lip is cheek or impudent talk

explanation.surface: An essay on Stoic philosophy claims its essential quality is firm, haughty rudeness.
explanation.definitionFit: Keeping a stiff upper lip is the idiom for enduring hardship without complaint, the essential Stoic virtue.

clue.text: Lively cheers following popular chief

indicators.note: the word for cheers comes after the other pieces

parts.note: something in fashion is in
high as in high priest, the chief one
spirits are drinks one raises with a cheers

explanation.surface: A cheerful boss is greeted with applause after being a hit.
explanation.definitionFit: In high spirits is an idiom for being cheerful and full of energy, much as lively suggests.

clue.text: Bad art is left in retreat, marvellous!

indicators.note: the letter for left goes inside the word for retreat

parts.note: to go back is to retreat
magic is informal for wonderful

explanation.surface: A critic finds poor artwork left hanging in a hideaway, and still calls it wonderful.
explanation.walkthrough: The art here is a sorcerer's, not a painter's: the black arts are evil magic.
explanation.definitionFit: Black magic is sorcery used for evil purposes, often called the black arts.

clue.text: Member burst a blood vessel rejecting female veggie?

parts.note: a leg is a limb, a member of the body

indicators.note: rejecting something casts it out of the word for losing one's temper

parts.note: to burst a blood vessel is to be furious, to fume

explanation.surface: Someone rages over a vegetarian who turns away a woman.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that veggie means a vegetable here, not a vegetarian.
explanation.definitionFit: Legumes are peas, beans and lentils, the pod vegetables of the pea family.

clue.text: Small fairy and raunchy Dame being successful by their own effort

definitions.text: being successful by their own effort

parts.note: an elf is a small fairy-like being

indicators.note: raunchy suggests wild, uninhibited behaviour, so these letters are tossed into a new order

parts.note: taken as written, these letters are the material to rearrange

explanation.surface: A tiny fairy and a racy pantomime dame make their own way to success.
explanation.walkthrough: A dame is a pantomime figure, a man in drag playing a comic older woman.
explanation.definitionFit: Self-made describes someone who achieved wealth or status through their own work, not inheritance.

clue.text: Be at odds with Republican getting into fancy ideas, e.g.

indicators.note: one piece getting into another goes inside it
fancy ideas are fanciful, elaborated ones, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written, the two letters of the abbreviation

explanation.surface: A Republican wades into some elaborate notions and disagrees with them.
explanation.definitionFit: To disagree is to hold a different opinion, the same as being in conflict with someone.

clue.text: Bit of leg: mostly poor stuff for cobblers?

parts.note: the calf is the back of the lower leg

indicators.note: mostly means all but the last letter of the word for poor

parts.note: skint is British slang for having no money

explanation.surface: Part of a leg is said to be mostly cheap material for shoemakers.
explanation.walkthrough: Cobblers is also British slang for nonsense, which the surface leans on; here it means shoemakers.
explanation.definitionFit: Calfskin is fine leather from a young cow, a material shoemakers use.

clue.text: Tight top left for prime of bodybuilders that's more stout

indicators.note: the letter for left stands in for the first letter of bodybuilders, which is dropped from the top

parts.note: a bustier is a close-fitting strapless top

indicators.note: the prime of something is its first letter

parts.note: the word whose first letter is the one to replace

explanation.surface: A tight vest is left out for the best of the bodybuilders, who are getting stockier.
explanation.walkthrough: Stout means sturdy and vigorous here, not fat.
explanation.definitionFit: Lustier means more vigorous and robust, a comparative of healthy strength like stouter.

clue.text: Jerks back clot in message

indicators.note: the reversed piece goes inside the message

parts.note: an SMS is a text message

indicators.note: back means the word for clot is read the other way

parts.note: a sap is a fool, as is a clot

explanation.surface: Some idiots send a reply that contains a stupid fool.
explanation.walkthrough: Clot is British slang for an idiot, not a blood clot.
explanation.definitionFit: Spasms are sudden involuntary muscle contractions, the twitches or jolts of the body.

clue.text: Fruit is a necessity when growing up

indicators.note: in a down answer, growing up means the pieces read from the bottom upward

parts.note: taken as written
a must is something essential
as in as I arrived, meaning when

explanation.surface: Eating fruit is essential for children while they grow.
explanation.definitionFit: A satsuma is a type of small, loose-skinned mandarin orange.

clue.text: Allow fictional AI character to become mortal

parts.note: to let is to allow
HAL is the murderous computer in 2001: A Space Odyssey

explanation.surface: A fictional computer is allowed to become human and mortal.
explanation.walkthrough: Mortal means deadly, as in a mortal wound, not a human being.
explanation.definitionFit: Lethal means fatal or deadly, as a mortal blow is.

clue.text: Confused men with name tags, I'm finding poor planning

indicators.note: letters that are confused are jumbled, so these words are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Bewildered men wearing name badges blame bad organisation.
explanation.definitionFit: Mismanagement is handling or running something badly, which poor planning amounts to.

clue.text: Man perhaps is what's central for valets

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: the central letters of the word valets are what is taken

parts.note: the word whose two middle letters are taken

explanation.surface: A manservant may be the key thing for those who work as valets.
explanation.walkthrough: Man is the Isle of Man, an island between Britain and Ireland, not a male person.
explanation.definitionFit: The Isle of Man is an island, so it is an example of an isle.

clue.text: German going round outside mill

indicators.note: the abbreviation for German goes round the other piece

parts.note: the rind is the outside layer of fruit or cheese

explanation.surface: A German walks around the outside of a mill.
explanation.definitionFit: A grinder is a machine that crushes things to powder, the job a mill does.

clue.text: Stockings used in blags

definitions.meaning: first meaning: stockings that stay up with elastic tops, no suspenders
second meaning: blags is British slang for robberies

explanation.surface: Robbers pull stockings over their faces for their raids.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both self-supporting hosiery and armed robberies, two unrelated senses of one compound.

clue.text: Eccentric sort lacking manners round King

indicators.note: the word for an ill-mannered sort goes round the abbreviation for king

parts.note: a cad is a man who behaves dishonourably
R is for Rex, Latin for king

explanation.surface: An odd, rude type surrounds the monarch.
explanation.definitionFit: A card is an amusing, odd character, an informal word for a funny or unusual person.

clue.text: Wrapping one of the strings near window husband grabbed

parts.note: the cello belongs to the strings section of an orchestra

indicators.note: the window seizes the husband's letter and holds it inside

parts.note: a pane is a sheet of window glass

explanation.surface: A husband snatches a cello near the window and wraps it up.
explanation.definitionFit: Cellophane is thin transparent film used for wrapping food and gifts, a packaging material.
